\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قبطان} (qubṭān)}{قبطان (qubṭān)}]{\ar{قبطان} (qubṭān) — a captain (of a ship)}

\label{lesson:AR-C429-qubtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the metro, then the Arabic for to unload.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قبطان}}
\textbf{\ar{قبطان}} — \emph{qubṭān} — \textquotedblleft{}a captain (of a ship)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلم} \ar{القبطان} \ar{مع} \ar{الركاب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallama al-qubṭān maʿa ar-rukkāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The captain spoke with the passengers.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قبطان}} (\emph{qubṭān}) was borrowed from Latin \emph{capitaneus}, \textquotedblleft{}a chief\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qubṭān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qubṭān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takallama al-qubṭān maʿa ar-rukkāb.} — The captain spoke with the passengers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for the metro, then the Arabic for to unload, then say \emph{qubṭān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{قبطان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A captain (of a ship)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قارب} (qārib)}{قارب (qārib)}]{\ar{قارب} (qārib) — a boat}

\label{lesson:AR-C429-qarib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to unload, then the Arabic for a captain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قارب}}
\textbf{\ar{قارب}} — \emph{qārib} — \textquotedblleft{}a boat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ركبنا} \ar{قاربا} \ar{صغيرا} \ar{إلى} \ar{الجزيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rakibnā qāriban ṣaghīran ilā al-jazīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We took a small boat to the island.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{قوارب}, \emph{qawārib}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قارب}} (\emph{qārib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be near\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane lists \emph{qārib} as a separate sense of the root: a ship's small boat, a skiff the seamen use for their errands.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to unload, then the Arabic for a captain, then say \emph{qārib} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عبارة} (ʿabbāra)}{عبارة (ʿabbāra)}]{\ar{عبارة} (ʿabbāra) — a ferry}

\label{lesson:AR-C429-abbara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a captain, then the Arabic for a boat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عبارة}}
\textbf{\ar{عبارة}} — \emph{ʿabbāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a ferry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عبرنا} \ar{النهر} \ar{بالعبارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿabarnā an-nahr bi-l-ʿabbāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We crossed the river by ferry.
\end{quote}

Unvocalized, the same letters spell \emph{ʿibāra}, \textquotedblleft{}a phrase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عبارة}} (\emph{ʿabbāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-b-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to cross\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{faʿʿāla} names a thing that does an action again and again: the crosser.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿabbāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿabbāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿabarnā an-nahr bi-l-ʿabbāra.} — We crossed the river by ferry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a captain, then the Arabic for a boat, then say \emph{ʿabbāra} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أبحر} (abḥara)}{أبحر (abḥara)}]{\ar{أبحر} (abḥara) — to sail; to set sail}

\label{lesson:AR-C429-abhara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a boat, then the Arabic for a ferry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أبحر}}
\textbf{\ar{أبحر}} — \emph{abḥara} — \textquotedblleft{}to sail; to set sail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أبحرت} \ar{السفينة} \ar{مع} \ar{الفجر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{abḥarat as-safīna maʿa al-fajr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The ship set sail at dawn.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يبحر}, \emph{yubḥir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أبحر}} (\emph{abḥara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-ḥ-r}, \textquotedblleft{}the sea\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to go out to sea\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رسا} (rasā)}{رسا (rasā)}]{\ar{رسا} (rasā) — to dock; to anchor}

\label{lesson:AR-C429-rasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a ferry, then the Arabic for to sail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رسا}}
\textbf{\ar{رسا}} — \emph{rasā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dock; to anchor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رست} \ar{السفينة} \ar{في} \ar{الميناء} \ar{بعد} \ar{الظهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rasat as-safīna fī al-mīnāʾ baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The ship docked in the port in the afternoon.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرسو}, \emph{yarsū}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رسا}} (\emph{rasā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-s-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be firm, fixed\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives it of a mountain standing firm and of a ship coming to anchor.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
